title: Five eras of UX design and the lessons to keep in the AI era
description: A comprehensive historical lens on six decades of UX evolution, distilled into lessons applicable to today's AI-driven design landscape. Essential context for understanding how past design paradigms can inform current and future challenges.

title: AI is making us build too much
description: A critical examination of how AI has made code, documentation, and organizational machinery cheap to produce—but expensive to maintain and own. This thought-provoking essay challenges the assumption that productivity gains always translate to better products, offering essential perspective for product leaders navigating AI-driven development.

title: Why products get worse
description: An insightful analysis of how companies systematically drain quality from products without triggering obvious metrics. This piece exposes the hidden mechanics behind product degradation—crucial reading for anyone concerned with long-term user satisfaction and sustainable design.

title: Building data-driven design systems
description: A practical case study on scaling design systems at Scribe to support 6 million users using data-driven principles. Packed with actionable strategies for design leaders looking to build robust, scalable design infrastructure.

title: 8 voice AIUX patterns
description: A systematic mapping of emerging voice AI interaction patterns, including agent roles, key design decisions, and limitations. Timely and practical for designers working on conversational AI experiences as voice becomes increasingly central to product interfaces.

title: How authentication friction frustrates users — and how to stop it
description: A practical guide to reducing authentication friction and improving security without sacrificing user experience. Directly applicable insights for product managers and designers seeking to streamline critical user flows.

title: Design Critique with Claude Code
description: A hands-on exploration of how Claude Code can be leveraged for design critique and feedback—moving beyond prototype generation to intelligent design evaluation. Relevant for designers exploring AI-assisted workflows and design collaboration.

title: Your first draft now has a log
description: A thought-provoking essay on workplace surveillance creeping into creative processes as AI monitors early-stage work. Important critical perspective for design leaders and organizations navigating ethics, trust, and creative autonomy in AI-augmented workflows.
